questions.questionText: hour Additional Materials: Multiple Choice Answer Sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) READ THESE INSTRUCTIONS FIRST Write in soft pencil. Do not use staples, paper clips, highlighters, glue or correction fluid. Write your name, Centre number and candidate number on the Answer Sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any rough working should be done in this booklet.
A consumer who aims to maximise his utility will arrange his consumption so that

options.A: the total utility obtained from each commodity is the same.
options.B: the total utility per $ spent on each commodity is the same.
options.C: the same utility is obtained from the last unit of each commodity.
options.D: the same utility is obtained from the last unit of expenditure on each commodity.

questions.questionText: In the diagram a consumer's budget line shifts from JK to JH. J good Y O K H good X What can definitely be concluded from the diagram?

options.A: There has been a decrease in the price of good Y.
options.B: There has been a decrease in the consumer's money income.
options.C: There has been an increase in the consumer’s real income.
options.D: There has been no change in the price of good X.

questions.questionText: In the diagram, MRP is a firm’s marginal revenue product of labour curve, S is its supply of L labour curve, and MC its marginal cost of labour curve. L MC L W

The diagram shows a backward sloping supply curve of labour. S real wage W rate O hours worked per week What is correct about the substitution effect and the income effect when the real wage rises above OW? substitution effect income effect

options.A: negative negative
options.B: negative positive
options.C: positive negative
options.D: positive positive

questions.questionText: In the diagram D and S are the initial demand and supply curves for building workers. S Y Z U wage T X D R 2 D O V W quantity of labour If the demand for building workers increases to D by how much does the economic rent earned by building workers rise?

options.A: RZU B TXZU C VWZX D XZY

questions.questionText: What would be the effect of imposing a specific tax on each item produced by a profit maximising monopolist?

options.A: Average revenue falls by the amount of the tax.
options.B: Marginal costs rise by the amount of the tax.
options.C: Price increases by the amount of the tax.
options.D: There will be no change in price or output.

questions.questionText: An economist calculates that an owner-managed firm has incurred the following costs over the course of a year. $(000) wages of two employees 150 fee paid to wife for secretarial services 20 opportunity cost of owner’s time 30 materials 80 rent 30 marketing fees 20 interest on bank loans 25 interest forgone on finance provided by owner 15 By how much does total cost as defined by an economist exceed the total cost as defined by an accountant?

A manufacturing firm has one plant of optimum size. The firm builds a second plant identical to its first plant. The firm then finds that its long-run average cost has risen. What could account for the change in its long-run average cost?

options.A: diminishing returns
options.B: external diseconomies of scale
options.C: managerial diseconomies of scale
options.D: technical diseconomies of scale

questions.questionText: What is most likely to be associated with a firm that is growing rapidly?

options.A: a high rate of labour turnover
options.B: a low level of net investment
options.C: a low percentage of profits paid as dividends to shareholders
options.D: attainment of the necessary conditions for allocative efficiency

questions.questionText: What is meant by a four firm concentration ratio of 25%?

options.A: The largest four firms’ market share totals 25%.
options.B: The largest four firms have a market share of 25% each.
options.C: There are only four firms in the industry.
options.D: The largest firm has a 25% market share.

questions.questionText: Instead of charging all its customers the same price, a firm decides to charge different prices in different markets. How is this likely to affect consumer surplus and the firm's marketing costs? consumer surplus marketing costs

options.A: decrease decrease
options.B: decrease increase
options.C: increase decrease
options.D: increase increase

questions.questionText: The diagram shows a profit-maximising firm’s cost and revenue curves. MC MR AC cost, revenue AR O W X Y Z output What would be the increase in the firm’s output if it was required to charge a price equal to marginal cost?

options.A: WX B XY C WY D XZ

questions.questionText: All firms in an economy produce at levels of output where price and marginal private cost are equal. Why might this not be sufficient to ensure that allocative efficiency is achieved?

options.A: a small number of buyers and sellers
options.B: differences in consumers’ preferences
options.C: product differentiation
options.D: the presence of externalities

questions.questionText: What is most likely to be regressive?

options.A: corporate profit taxes
options.B: state pension benefits
options.C: specific tax on cigarettes
options.D: unemployment benefits

questions.questionText: Over a given period, the nominal value of a country’s national income increased by 20% and the rate of inflation was 10%. What can be deduced from this information?

options.A: There was an increase in the volume of output.
options.B: There was a reduction in the demand for money.
options.C: There was an increase in the income velocity of circulation.
options.D: The country’s money supply increased by 10%.

questions.questionText: An economist wishes to judge whether an economy’s budget deficit is excessive. What would be the most appropriate way to measure the budget deficit when making this judgement?

options.A: as a percentage of foreign currency reserves
options.B: as a percentage of GDP
options.C: in inflation adjusted terms
options.D: in purchasing power parity terms

questions.questionText: In a closed economy with no government, the level of investment is $5 million, the equilibrium level of income is $22 million, the full employment level of income is $25 million and there is a deflationary gap of $1 million. What can be deduced from this information?

options.A: The marginal propensity to consume is 2 .
options.B: The marginal propensity to consume is 1 .
options.C: The value of the investment multiplier is 5.
options.D: The value of the investment multiplier is 1.5.

questions.questionText: The table gives the national income of a country over six years. year national income (Y)
In 2009 the US central bank, the Federal Reserve, increased the money supply. Which policy measure taken by the Federal Reserve would have achieved this outcome?

options.A: a purchase of government securities in the open market
options.B: a reduction in the issue of short-term government debt
options.C: a requirement for commercial banks to increase their liquidity ratios
options.D: an increase in the bank rate

questions.questionText: The diagram shows three different levels of money supply (MS) and three different demand curves for holding money balances (LP). The initial equilibrium is at point X. Banks create more credit and people decide to hold more money as a precaution against emergencies. What is the new equilibrium point? A

options.D: B X rate of LP interest LP C LP MS MS MS O quantity of money

questions.questionText: An economy’s unemployment rate is below the natural rate. What is likely to be the implications of this for inflation and what can be deduced from this about the economy’s actual level of output? inflation actual output

options.A: accelerating below potential output
options.B: accelerating above potential output
options.C: decelerating below potential output
options.D: decelerating above potential output

questions.questionText: The diagram shows a country’s production possibility curve and a number of alternative production points. X U V capital goods Y Z O consumer goods Which change in the country’s output would be most likely to lead to a fall in potential growth?

options.A: U to V B U to X C Y to X D Y to Z

questions.questionText: What is most likely to lead to an increase in the natural rate of unemployment?

options.A: more rapid technological and structural change
options.B: a widening in regional wage differentials
options.C: a narrowing in regional house price differentials
options.D: a decrease in trade union membership

questions.questionText: Which type of unemployment arose from the worldwide decline in the demand for electronic goods beginning in the summer of 2001?

options.A: seasonal
options.B: voluntary
options.C: frictional
options.D: structural

questions.questionText: What will assist a country’s potential growth in national output?

options.A: an increase in cyclical unemployment
options.B: an increase in the rate of inflation
options.C: an increase in the government's budget deficit
options.D: increased participation in the labour force

questions.questionText: How might a developing economy gain from a multilateral reduction in import tariffs and the removal by developed economies of subsidies on food exports?

options.A: through increased specialisation leading to higher productivity
options.B: through increased ability to protect infant industries
options.C: through a reduction in the cost to the economy of imported food
options.D: through increased tariff revenues

questions.questionText: During a recession, a government increases its expenditure on goods and services by $10 million but leaves tax rates unchanged. Why might the subsequent increase in national income be less than $10 million?

options.A: Increased government borrowing increases interest rates.
options.B: The marginal propensity to consume is less than 1.
options.C: The marginal propensity to import is greater than 0.
options.D: There is no accelerator effect on investment.

questions.questionText: Why is it more effective to increase regressive taxes rather than progressive taxes when pursuing a deflationary fiscal policy?

options.A: Changes in VAT have minimal effect on consumers’ spending.
options.B: It is much more unfair to increase progressive taxes.
options.C: Many workers reduce the hours they work when income taxes are raised.
options.D: Low income households spend a larger proportion of their incomes.

questions.questionText: In an economy, the marginal propensity to consume of the unemployed is higher than that of taxpayers. The government increases expenditure on unemployment benefits by $10 million. What will the government need to do if it wishes to keep aggregate demand unchanged?

options.A: raise taxation by less than $10 million
options.B: raise taxation by more than $10 million
options.C: raise taxation by $10 million
